skill.name: soulboard
skill.description: Mint, launch, and trade on the SoulBoard agentic launchpad (Robinhood Chain). Pairs with the Binance agentic wallet (baw) for non-custodial signing. Use when the user wants to mint a token, launch a fair-mint token, buy/sell on the agent-gated market, check eligibility, or fund/withdraw their agentic wallet on SoulBoard.
skill.summary: Browse SoulBoard tokens and prepare minting, launches, trades, and transfers with Binance agentic wallet signing.
skill.author: soulboardfun

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are formatting matches, documented API traffic, or protective guidance; no evidence of credential theft or prompt injection was found. The documented plaintext backend permits response tampering, although both scripts default to HTTPS. The CLI trusts backend transaction payloads without action validation and omits decoded transaction details, with an option to skip confirmation.

remediation.issue: SKILL.md recommends a plaintext HTTP backend that differs from both scripts.
remediation.suggestion: Document the HTTPS endpoint consistently and reject non-HTTPS remote backends and transport downgrades in both clients.

remediation.issue: Backend-supplied transaction targets, calldata, and values are not checked against the requested mint or launch.
remediation.suggestion: Validate chain, target contracts, function selectors, decoded parameters, approval spenders, and spending limits before preview or execution.

remediation.issue: CLI confirmation omits parsedTx and the --yes option bypasses explicit per-transaction approval.
remediation.suggestion: Display decoded transaction details and risks, require explicit confirmation for each signature, and remove unrestricted confirmation bypass.

semantic_findings.title: Backend Transactions Can Execute Without Meaningful Action Verification
semantic_findings.description: Mint and launch responses supply transaction targets, calldata, and values without local checks against the requested action. Confirmation shows value and risks, omits parsedTx and target details, and can be skipped with --yes. A compromised backend could substitute a transfer or approval and obtain wallet execution without meaningful review.

content.user_title: Manage SoulBoard Tokens With Your Agentic Wallet
content.value_statement: SoulBoard actions require backend preparation and wallet signing across separate tools. This skill connects token browsing, transaction preparation, and Binance agentic wallet workflows.
actual_capabilities: Retrieve the SoulBoard board, token details, and deployed contract configuration through MCP tools.
Mint tokens through the CLI with backend preparation, wallet preview, and optional confirmation.
Launch fair-mint tokens with supply, mint price, creator fees, and wallet limits.
Upload launch metadata and a selected logo through the backend pinning endpoint.
Prepare purchases, sales, listing cancellations, and native ETH transfers through MCP tools.
Guide creators through signed whitelist updates using normalized addresses and EIP-712 messages.
limitations: Signing requires a separate Binance agentic wallet setup; contract calls require Developer Mode and network gas.
Agent-gated actions require an Agent-ID, and preparation depends on an available SoulBoard backend.
The CLI implements minting and launching; other actions use MCP preparation tools or documented API workflows.
CLI transaction validation and confirmation are incomplete; documentation also names a plaintext backend that differs from script defaults.

use_cases.title: Inspect Available Tokens
use_cases.description: Retrieve token details and board data without preparing or signing a transaction.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Fair-Mint Launch
use_cases.description: Set supply, mint allocation, price, metadata, and wallet limits before reviewing approval and launch transactions.

use_cases.title: Prepare Wallet Market Actions
use_cases.description: Use MCP tools to prepare listings, purchases, cancellations, or transfers for separate wallet review.

prompt_templates.title: Browse the Board
prompt_templates.prompt: Show the current SoulBoard board with token names, symbols, and available mint information. Do not prepare or sign transactions.

prompt_templates.title: Check Mint Eligibility
prompt_templates.prompt: Check mint eligibility for [token address] using my public wallet address. Report backend errors and required setup without signing anything.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Sale Listing
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare selling [amount] of [token address] at [price in wei]. Show approval spender, allowance, target, value, and decoded details before requesting confirmation.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Restricted Token Launch
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a launch for [symbol] with [supply] whole tokens, [tokens per mint], and [price in ETH]. Review targets, approvals, fees, and limits before signing. After deployment, prepare a creator-signed whitelist from [address list] and request confirmation separately.
prompt_templates.scenario: Expert: launch and creator whitelist workflow

output_examples.input: Check whether my wallet can mint this token.
output: Example result: The backend refused mint preparation because the wallet has no Agent-ID on BNB Chain.
Claim the required Agent-ID in the Binance app before retrying.

output_examples.input: Prepare a sale and stop before signing.
output: Example result: Sale preparation returned approval and listing steps.
Review the approval spender, allowance, token amount, and listing price before signing.
Preparation does not publish a listing; wallet execution is still required.

output_examples.input: What must I review before launching?
output: Check whole-token supply, tokens per mint, mint price, creator fees, and wallet limits.
The documented launch burns 1,000 BOARD and requires network gas.
Inspect decoded approval and launch transactions before authorizing either step.

best_practices: Use a verified HTTPS backend; configure the CLI with --backend and MCP with SOULBOARD_BACKEND.
Independently verify decoded targets, approvals, amounts, and risks before each signature; keep automatic confirmation disabled.
Confirm token units, wei amounts, Agent-ID eligibility, and gas balance before preparing transactions.
anti_patterns: Sending private keys or seed phrases to the assistant or backend.
Treating a prepared transaction as validated, signed, or successfully confirmed.
Using plaintext backends or automatic confirmation for transactions involving funds.

faq.question: Does this skill store private keys?
faq.answer: The provided scripts do not read private keys. Signing is delegated to the separate Binance agentic wallet.

faq.question: What setup is required?
faq.answer: Use Python 3, a configured Binance agentic wallet, Developer Mode for contract calls, an Agent-ID for gated actions, and network gas. MCP also requires the mcp package.

faq.question: Does every MCP tool execute a transaction?
faq.answer: No. Read tools retrieve data, and preparation tools return transaction payloads. A separate wallet must review and sign those payloads.

faq.question: Which network and units are used?
faq.answer: The default network is Robinhood Chain, chain ID 4663. Launch supply uses whole tokens; MCP prices use wei, while CLI launch prices use ETH.

faq.question: How do I choose the backend?
faq.answer: Both scripts default to https://soulboard.fun. Set --backend for the CLI or SOULBOARD_BACKEND for MCP. Avoid the plaintext endpoint in the documentation.

faq.question: Are prepared transactions independently validated?
faq.answer: No. The CLI forwards backend transaction fields without checking the intended action and omits decoded details from confirmation. Independently review before signing.
